subject: medicine
title: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia and Vitamin D Toxicity

steps.tx: Inherited predisposition syndromes caused by autosomal dominant mutations orchestrate synchronized neuroendocrine neoplasia across multiple organ systems. Characterized by the classical triad of pituitary, parathyroid, and pancreatic islet tumours, **men 1** (Wermer syndrome) stems from inactivating germline mutations in the MEN1 tumour suppressor gene encoding menin. Primary hyperparathyroidism represents the earliest and most penetrant manifestation, affecting over ninety-five percent of gene carriers by age fifty. It typically presents with multiglandular parathyroid hyperplasia rather than a solitary adenoma, predisposing to recurrent hypercalcaemia.
steps.say: Inherited predisposition syndromes caused by autosomal dominant mutations orchestrate synchronized neuroendocrine tumours across multiple systems. Primary hyperparathyroidism represents the earliest and most penetrant manifestation, affecting over ninety-five percent of gene carriers. It typically presents with multiglandular hyperplasia rather than a solitary adenoma, risking recurrent hypercalcaemia.

steps.tx: Gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations produce a distinct familial syndrome featuring medullary thyroid carcinoma and phaeochromocytoma. Designated as **men 2a** (Sipple syndrome), this autosomal dominant condition is driven by germline activating missense mutations in the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11. Nearly one hundred percent of gene carriers develop multifocal, bilateral medullary thyroid carcinoma. Roughly fifty percent develop phaeochromocytomas, and twenty to thirty percent develop primary parathyroid hyperplasia. Early prophylactic total thyroidectomy in childhood is mandatory based on RET mutation risk stratification.
steps.say: Gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations produce a distinct familial syndrome featuring medullary thyroid carcinoma and phaeochromocytoma. Designated as men 2a, this autosomal dominant condition is driven by activating mutations in the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome ten. Nearly all gene carriers develop bilateral medullary thyroid carcinoma arising from calcitonin-secreting C cells. Roughly half develop phaeochromocytomas, and thirty percent develop parathyroid hyperplasia. Prophylactic total thyroidectomy is performed in childhood.

steps.tx: A highly aggressive variant of hereditary neuroendocrine neoplasia pairs lethal early-onset medullary carcinoma with characteristic physical stigmata. Manifesting without parathyroid involvement, **men 2b** (Gorlin syndrome) is driven by specific RET codon M918T mutations in over ninety-five percent of cases. Medullary thyroid carcinoma develops within the first year of life with rapid, early lymphatic and hematogenous metastasis, necessitating prophylactic total thyroidectomy in infancy. Striking physical stigmata include a marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas on the lips and anterior tongue, thickened corneal nerve fibres, and intestinal ganglioneuromatosis causing severe chronic constipation or megacolon.
steps.say: A highly aggressive variant of hereditary neuroendocrine neoplasia pairs lethal early-onset medullary carcinoma with characteristic physical stigmata. Manifesting without parathyroid involvement, men 2b is driven by specific RET codon M918T mutations in most cases. Medullary thyroid carcinoma develops within the first year of life with early metastasis, requiring prophylactic thyroidectomy in infancy. Physical stigmata include a marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas on the lips and tongue, and intestinal ganglioneuromatosis.

right.title: MEN 2B Phenotype
points: Aggressive medullary thyroid carcinoma in infancy

steps.tx: Exogenous hypervitaminosis driven by excessive ingestion of fat-soluble secosteroids produces severe hypercalcaemia with suppressed parathyroid hormone. Developing **vitamin d intoxication** occurs when mega-doses of ergocalciferol or cholecalciferol overwhelm hepatic 25-hydroxylase and circulating binding capacity. Marked elevations of circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D directly stimulate enterocyte calcium absorption and mobilize skeletal mineral. Laboratory profiling reveals hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, hyperphosphataemia, suppressed intact PTH, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels exceeding one hundred and fifty nanograms per millilitre. Because vitamin D stores in adipose tissue, toxicity persists for weeks, responding to volume repletion, loop diuretics, and systemic glucocorticoids.
steps.say: Exogenous hypervitaminosis driven by excessive ingestion of fat-soluble vitamins produces severe hypercalcaemia with suppressed parathyroid hormone. Developing vitamin d intoxication occurs when mega-doses of cholecalciferol overwhelm hepatic enzymes and circulating binding capacity. Marked elevations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D stimulate enterocyte calcium absorption and bone resorption. Laboratory profiling reveals hypercalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, suppressed intact PTH, and high vitamin D levels. Therapy includes saline rehydration, loop diuretics, and glucocorticoids.

nodes.label: Massive vitamin D ingestion: Serum 25-OH-D > 150 ng/mL
Excessive gut Ca2+ and PO4- absorption + osteoclast resorption
Treatment: Isotonic saline, furosemide, and oral Prednisone (40 mg/day)

steps.tx: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours in MEN 1 exhibit diverse secretory patterns and unpredictable malignant potential. The most common functional enteropancreatic neoplasm is gastrinoma, leading to severe Zollinger-Ellison syndrome with refractory, recurrent peptic ulcers. The second most frequent is insulinoma, causing episodic fasting neuroglycopenic hypoglycaemia. Glucagonomas provoke necrolytic migratory erythema, while VIPomas trigger profuse watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia, and achlorhydria (Verner-Morrison syndrome). In contrast to sporadic single adenomas, **enteropancreatic tumours** in MEN 1 are characteristically multiple, multifocal, and scattered throughout the duodenum and pancreatic parenchyma, complicating curative surgical resection.

Glucagonomas provoke necrolytic migratory erythema, while VIPomas trigger profuse watery diarrhoea and hypokalaemia. Enteropancreatic tumours in MEN 1 are characteristically multiple, multifocal, and scattered throughout the duodenum and pancreas.

steps.tx: Surgical management of multiglandular parathyroid disease in MEN 1 mandates balancing recurrence prevention against permanent hypoparathyroidism. Because all four parathyroid glands possess the germline mutation, leaving normal tissue risks late recurrent hyperparathyroidism. Performing **subtotal parathyroidectomy** with resection of three and a half glands, or total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation into the forearm brachioradialis muscle, represents the standard surgical strategy. If hypercalcaemia recurs years later, a portion of the autotransplanted tissue can be excised under local anaesthesia in the forearm, avoiding reoperative cervical exploration.

nodes.label: Recurrence managed easily via minor forearm excision under local anaesthesia

steps.tx: Surveillance protocols for asymptomatic mutation carriers ensure early detection of lethal neuroendocrine neoplasms before distant metastatic dissemination. Genetic testing for **ret mutations** is recommended for all first-degree relatives of MEN 2 probands. Carriers of high-risk mutations (codons 634 or 918) undergo prophylactic total thyroidectomy in early childhood, monitored by serial serum calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen. Prior to any neck surgery, clinicians must rigorously exclude coexisting phaeochromocytoma via plasma fractionated metanephrines, because administering general anaesthesia in unblocked phaeochromocytoma precipitates fatal intraoperative hypertensive crisis.

left.title: Rule of Priority in MEN 2 Surgery
points: Screen for phaeochromocytoma BEFORE neck surgery
If phaeochromocytoma present, resect ADRENAL FIRST
Alpha-blockade with phenoxybenzamine prior to surgery

steps.tx: Differentiating hypercalcaemia etiologies across complex metabolic syndromes relies on integrating intact hormone, metabolite, and imaging findings. Intact parathyroid hormone is elevated in MEN 1 and primary hyperparathyroidism, but suppressed in vitamin D intoxication and humoral malignancy. Serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is elevated in sarcoidosis and lymphoma, whereas 25-hydroxyvitamin D is elevated in exogenous toxicity. Comprehensive assessment of serum phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and urinary calcium guides targeted pharmacological therapy, preserving renal filtration and skeletal **bone density**.
steps.say: Differentiating hypercalcaemia etiologies across complex syndromes relies on integrating intact hormone, metabolite, and imaging findings. Intact parathyroid hormone is elevated in MEN 1 and primary hyperparathyroidism, but suppressed in vitamin D toxicity and humoral malignancy. Serum calcitriol is elevated in sarcoidosis and lymphoma, whereas 25-hydroxyvitamin D is elevated in exogenous toxicity. Assessment of phosphate and urinary calcium guides targeted therapy, preserving renal filtration and bone density.
